newsitem.title: CANADA: Kenting CEO says Precision bid a surprise.
newsitem.headline: Kenting CEO says Precision bid a surprise.

text.p: The president and chief executive of Canada's newest publicly traded oil drilling company said on Monday he was surprised by a swift attempt to take the firm over.
Kenting Energy Services Inc, in the process of being spun off by Trimac Ltd, became a takeover target for Precision Drilling Corp before its shares were priced and started trading.
"Obviously this is a surprise and obviously it's very opportunistic before we've established a price for our own stock," said Kenting's Tim Swinton.
"And we had a very interesting acquisition that we've announced."

Swinton said he was unable to comment further until his firm considered all the facts. Kenting, which had been part of Trimac's stable of businesses, had been rumored as a target for high-flying Precision.

Precision said on Monday it would offer C$3.50 cash plus a tenth of one of its shares, unless Precision stock exceeded C$70 a share on the day before the bid's expiry date. If Precision shares rose above C$70, the value of exchange would be a maximum of C$7, it said.
If the deal was successful, Precision would own 34 percent of the drilling rigs operating in Canada, it said.
The company also said that the offer was contingent on there being no material change to Kenting's assets or share capital.
However, Kenting and Lynx Energy Services Corp said on Monday that Lynx had completed the sale of eight drilling rigs to Kenting for C$18.3 million and the two firms planned a merger of their own.
Under that deal, Lynx shareholders would receive 7.3 million Kenting shares.
Lynx said that, after the proposed transactions, each of its shareholders would receive about 1.2 Kenting shares and Kenting would continue Lynx's drilling businesses.
Shareholders would also receive equity interest in a new public company comprising the rest of Lynx's businesses, it said.
